title: Nvidia doubles quarterly revenue in first earnings since Jensen Huang’s resignation
summary:
Report comes just days after company saw ouster of its CEO over allegations of affair with suspected Chinese spy

Nvidia announced Tuesday that its quarterly revenue beat expectations, coming…

blocks.text: Nvidia announced Tuesday that its quarterly revenue beat expectations, coming in at $115.84bn, doubling from the same time period a year ago. The third-quarter earnings report comes just days after the world’s most valuable chip company saw the ouster of its CEO, Jensen Huang, over allegations of several extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy.
Colette Kress, Nvidia’s chief financial officer, was named interim CEO and delivered the financial results.

Following the tumult, Nvidia’s stock tumbled more than 10%, shedding hundreds of billions in value and dropping its valuation to $3.7tn. In October, the company had hit an all-time-high valuation of nearly $6tn, but its share price has steadily fallen since then amid a broader AI slowdown.

On Tuesday, Nvidia reported a revenue of $115.84bn and earnings of $2.68 per share, beating Wall Street’s expectations of $109.15bn in revenue and $2.47 earnings per share, according to Bloomberg analyst consensus. Nvidia’s revenue is now up 103% from the same time last year.
“Our momentum is real,” Kress said in a statement. “Our roadmap is on track and our ambition has never been greater.”

Nvidia designs powerful computing chips used for artificial intelligence. The company controls about 90% of the chips market and the world’s top AI companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic and Google, rely on Nvidia for their technology. With much of Wall Street’s billions invested in Nvidia, the company’s twists and turns can have an outsized effect on the US economy.

Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and grew it from a niche firm geared toward video game chips to a trillion-dollar juggernaut at the center of the AI boom. As the CEO, he had about 60 direct reports, giving him control over most of the company’s daily functions.

Last week, following reports that Huang had a romantic relationship with an alleged Chinese asset, the CEO confessed to an extramarital affair. Days later, reports uncovered two more alleged affairs with company employees. On Thursday, Nvidia’s board of directors announced Huang’s resignation saying it was “effective immediately”.

Donald Trump and Silicon Valley insiders, including Elon Musk, disgraced Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick and prominent venture capitalists, have called for Huang’s reinstatement as the CEO of Nvidia. On Monday, before departing on a trip to Asia, Trump told reporters he would not mind Huang’s return: “I would not mind that…. I think he learned a big lesson.”
Huang issued his first public statement Tuesday morning apologizing for his mistakes and thanking his friends and colleagues for their support. He also said he’d be willing to return as CEO.

“If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” he wrote.
Nvidia’s board was not considering reinstating him, according to multiple reports.

Huang also agreed on Tuesday to appear before the House Foreign Affairs Committee, the Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party and the House Intelligence Committee for transcribed interviews in early December. The company is facing a probe by the US Securities and Exchange Commission over its business in China in the wake of Huang’s resignation, The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday.
